title: Adapting open-source drone autopilots for real-time iceberg observations
author: Carlson, Rysgaard

steps.title: Prepare equipment and power source
steps.instruction: Gather the APM autopilot assembly, EXITE beacon, small boat (8 m length), boat hook, power supply, and a laptop with QGC (or Mission Planner/APM Planner) installed.

steps.title: Power on APM before departure
steps.instruction: Turn on the APM in the morning before leaving the harbor; keep it powered for the entire field day and power it off at the end of the ~10 h test period.

steps.title: Deploy APM and EXITE on iceberg
steps.instruction: Maneuver the 8 m boat next to the 80 m‑long iceberg, slide the APM assembly (mounted on a 1.2 m wooden slat) onto the ice, and hand‑deploy the EXITE beacon on the same iceberg. Record that the EXITE beacon is positioned 7–16 m from the APM.

steps.title: Collect telemetry data
steps.instruction: Start data acquisition; the APM will log telemetry at 1–5 Hz for approximately 70 minutes while air temperature is 5–8 °C. Monitor the link and be prepared for a possible ~15‑minute communication gap; mitigate future gaps by raising the ground‑station antenna elevation.

steps.title: Perform CTD casts
steps.instruction: While the boat drifts, conduct seven CTD profiles with the CastAway CTD (embedded GPS) from the surface down to ~25 m depth (water column depth ≈600 m). Suspend a cast when the APM‑base data link is lost and resume after it is re‑established. Use the common GPS time stamps to compute the distance between each CTD location and the APM; distances will range from 13 m to 130 m.

steps.title: Retrieve APM assembly
steps.instruction: Snag one of the APM ropes with the boat hook and pull the assembly back onto the boat. Note that the assembly remained fixed to the ice as the aluminum cross‑bar melted and did not refreeze.

steps.title: Export telemetry log to CSV
steps.instruction: Open the .tlog file in QGC (or Mission Planner/APM Planner) and export it as a .csv file for further analysis.

steps.title: Convert GPS to UTM
steps.instruction: In Matlab, use the ‘deg2utm’ function (WGS84 datum) to convert the GPS latitude/longitude coordinates to UTM coordinates.

steps.title: Average position and orientation
steps.instruction: Compute ten‑second averages of the position (UTM) and orientation data (pitch, roll, heading) from the exported CSV.

steps.title: Calculate iceberg kinematics
steps.instruction: From the averaged UTM positions, calculate linear velocity and acceleration using central‑difference schemes; discard magnetic heading data due to anomalies. Compute pitch, roll, and angular acceleration rates. Expect iceberg speeds of 0–0.1 m s⁻¹, an acceleration event around 25 minutes into the test, and a gradual tilt observable in pitch/roll.
